title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-17
content:
Morning checklist (quick)
- 09:00 standup notes: bandwidth tickets piling up for eu-west1. Riley to follow up with cloud partner.
- On-call handoff 17:00 -> Priya (reminder to leave clear notes)

TODAY'S PRIORITY
1) Validate node pool scaling policy for gpu-pool-prod (observed saturation at 75% during 20:00\u201322:00). If autoscaler does not add nodes, fallback to burst-policy-2.
   - action: run `kubectl get hpa -n infra gpu-inference` and check events
   - action: review ASG/instance group scaling diagnostics: check last 3 scale events (cloud console)
   - note: if scale delay > 120s, toggle aggressive-scaler (temp) and monitor latency for 30m
2) Investigate intermittent OOMs on nvcache nodes (nvcache-2a/b). Suspect kernel patch from 2026-02-28.
   - grep dmesg for oom_killer, nvlink errors: `journalctl -u nvcache.service | grep -i oom`
   - rollback kernel on one canary node (nvcache-2b) and re-run repro workload (mini-bench)
   - link: GH PR org/redwood/nvdriver#22 (kernel pinning change)
3) Network MTU mismatch in eu-west1: trunks report 1500 vs 9000 on some hosts -> packet drops for RPCs to redis-cluster-3
   - temp workaround: reduce jumbo mtu to 1500 for affected azs until infra team schedules maintenance
   - ticket: JIRA NET-711 (assigned to Marco)

QUICK NOTES / TODOS
- Add capacity target numbers to Friday ops report: include per-region GPU available (p100/v100/a100), reserved vs free, expected commit for next 30d. (Est 1h)
- Follow up w/finance re: Dedicated customer burst credits (how to show in billing dashboard) -> Slack #billing
- Update runbook: "gpu-eviction-handling" with steps to drain pods gracefully, announce on /infra-alerts before running.
- PR to infra repo: add alert for GPU node saturation > 70% for 15m (current is 90%) -> open PR and request Priya review.

INCIDENT BITS (from last night)
- 02:14: high latency on hosted-api -> traced to eu-west1 redis failover + queued requests hitting nvcache cold start.
- Mitigation: increased concurrency limit on fallback model to reduce queue depth, set cache warmers for 3 popular prefixes.
- Postmortem draft TODO (start): timeline, RCA (nvcache OOM + redis failover), mitigations (kernel rollback, MTU fix, warmers).

COMMANDS / CHECKS I RAN
- `kubectl -n infra describe pod nvcache-2b | grep -i oom` -> no immediate kill recorded on canary after restart
- `aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-prod-asg | tail -n 20` -> last scale event 2026-03-02 21:02 (manual)
- `redis-cli -h redis-cluster-3.cluster.eu-west1 GET some:key` -> occasional timeouts (~120ms)

DECISIONS/OPEN QUESTIONS
- Do we permanently lower obj store replication factor for logs to reduce network egress? (tradeoff: less durability)
- Should we accelerate rollout of NVLink driver pin across all nvcache nodes or run staggered canary? Prefer staggered but need timeline.

FOLLOW-UPS FOR TOMORROW
- Schedule 30m sync with Marco (network) to finalise MTU change window.
- Run a controlled kernel rollback on nvcache-2a after conversation with SRE team.
- Add sample queries to cache-warmer job config (top 100 prefixes by qps).

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep notes minimal in this doc; move final runbook edits to confluence page and link here.
- If touching autoscaler, notify product routes team (they might see extra latency).
- Remember to annotate PRs with `ops/urgent` if they affect production scaling.

RANDOM SHORTHANDS (for copy/paste)
- HPA check: `kubectl get hpa -n infra gpu-inference -o yaml`
- Drain cmd: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- Canary rollback: `ssh ops@nvcache-2b sudo apt-get install linux-image-<version>` (document exact version in runbook)

END
